newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks close lower on Wall St's plunge.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks close lower on Wall St's plunge.

text.p: Tokyo stocks closed lower on Monday, as the Dow Industrials' plunge on Friday hammered local shares, particularly those in the high-technology sector, brokers said.

The Dow's impact on Tokyo stocks was limited by a view that its tumble on Friday was a natural correction after a long rally, brokers said, adding that they would watch Monday's New York market closely.
The 225-share Nikkei average shed 284.93 points or 1.47 percent to close at 19,041.10.
The index briefly dropped as low as 18,835.48.
Nikkei September futures closed 440 points lower at 19,000.

"I expect the effect from the tumble in New York to be limited, as it was a healthy correction after a long winning streak," said Hitoshi Morimura, chief portfolio manager at Meiji Life Insurance Company.
Analysts said they would pay more attention to the strength of the Japanese economy.
"The Japanese market is currently vulnerable to negative news because of the shaky recovery in the domestic economy," said Keiko Kondo, a strategist at Merrill Lynch Japan Inc.
She said sentiment towards the economy has to improve before the Nikkei average can head higher.
"Export-driven shares have been leading the market, but unless domestic-demand reliant issues generate a rally, the market overall is not likely to turn upward," Morimura said.

Given the weakness of Japan's economic recovery after the consumption tax was raised in April and the payoff scandal involving top brokerages, the Nikkei 225 index is likely to slip below a recent low of 18,801.68 marked on Wednesday, investors and analysts said.
Turnover remained light at 360 million shares on the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange (TSE) against 422 million shares on Friday. This was partly due to the summer holidays.
Declining issues outnumbered advancers 776 to 314, while 143 issues were unchanged.
The broader-based TOPIX index dropped 11.40 points or 0.76 percent to finish at 1,490.29. The Nikkei 300 average fell 2.33 points or 0.79 percent to 291.82.
On Friday, the Dow tumbled 247.37 points to 7,694.66, its second-biggest point drop ever.
Analysts in Tokyo said the blue-chip index is unlikely to post further sharp losses in the near future, as there are little signs of inflation in the United States amid the robust economic growth.

"Friday's sharp fall in New York appears to be an adjustment after rapid gains," said Tsuyoshi Kawada, a market analyst at Nikko Research Centre. "The fall itself will not raise serious concerns as there are no strong signs of inflation in the United States."
Among the high-technology shares that were affected by the sharp retreat in New York was electronics giant Sony Corp, which lost 400 yen to end at 11,500 yen.
Shares of chip equipment makers also slid, with Advantest Corp losing 400 yen to 12,300 and Tokyo Electron Ltd sinking 330 yen to 7,650.

Shares of construction firm Fujita Corp jumped on the Tokyo bourse, cheered by its restructuring plan. They were up 16 yen or 17.78 percent at 106 yen, making the firm the second-largest percentage gainer. Fujita said it had formed a plan covering the period to March 31, 2000 and its major creditor Sakura Bank had said it would accept the plan.

Losing sectors were led by mining, warehousing, and pulp/paper, and rubber. The major gainers were railway/bus and electric power. The second section index ended down 17.04 points at 1,663.08. The over-the-counter (OTC) index was up 0.24 point at 1,065.09.
-- Hiroko Nakata, Tokyo Equities Desk
